title: The AI Boom’s Hidden Cost: Wholesale Prices Are Surging 41% in America’s Largest Electricity Market
key_facts: The US Energy Information Administration's October Short-Term Energy Outlook forecasts 2026 wholesale electricity prices in PJM, the country's largest power market, up 41% from 2025.
That is the largest forecast rise of any region EIA tracks; average US wholesale prices are expected to rise 11% to $52 per megawatt-hour, and Northwest Mid-Columbia prices to fall 23%.
EIA attributes much of this year's increase to weather (unusually hot summer, winter storms), so data centres explain only part of the 41%.
Household bills move separately because retail rates also include transmission, distribution, capacity costs and regulatory decisions.
EIA projects commercial demand, which includes data centres, to grow 2.8% in 2027 and industrial demand 2.7%.
The rest of the article is an investment case for Quanta Services (revenue up 41.1% in Q2 2026) and other grid suppliers.
